extracted.intended_audience: research-integrity community, journal editors, researchers, and clinicians following retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and assessing grounds, processes, and transparency in journal retraction notices and related investigations (illustrated by a high-profile anesthesiology case). Useful for editors, integrity officers, and researchers tracking retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction due to falsified data
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors ... hereby withdraw the article ... with regard to falsified data and the subsequent recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Falsified data uncovered by an investigation is explicit grounds for retraction; publisher/editor statements should cite falsification as the reason. In this case the journal retracted after an institutional review recommended withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction based on discrepancies between published articles and doctoral theses
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions were based on allegations about discrepancies in the data between the articles published in Der Anaesthesist and doctorate theses submitted at the University of Giessen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies between a paper’s data and related primary documents (e.g., theses) can justify retraction even decades after publication; such documentary mismatches are legitimate evidence of unreliable findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional investigation and recommendation as the evidentiary basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The retraction notice cites an investigation by Justus Liebig University Gießen and the university’s subsequent recommendation as the basis for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and publishers may rely on formal institutional investigations and their recommendations when deciding to retract. A clear link between the investigating body and the retraction decision strengthens legitimacy of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor/publisher should attempt to contact corresponding and co-authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence author of the article J. Boldt did not react to the contact of the editors and the publisher ... the other authors ... could no longer be found due to the time difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction procedures should include attempts to contact the corresponding author and co-authors; notices should document attempts and outcomes (e.g., no response, unable to locate). Time elapsed since publication can make locating authors difficult—documenting that is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of retraction notices (state reason and source)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors of Der Anaesthesist and Springer Medizin Verlag withdraw the article based on an investigation ... with regard to falsified data and the subsequent recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction notices should state the substantive reason for retraction (e.g., falsified data), identify the investigating institution or source of the finding, and provide sufficient detail for readers to understand the grounds. Providing translations or clarifications (when notices are in another language) and updating public statements when new information emerges are good practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of patient/public-safety harm in assessing misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldt’s misconduct ... is believed to have put at risk the lives of potentially millions of patients by overstating the safety and effectiveness of certain volume expanders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When misconduct affects clinical recommendations or patient safety, the severity of harm is a critical factor in the response (retraction, notification, possible regulatory or legal action). Notices and commentary should acknowledge potential public-health impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness: long delays between publication and retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The new retractions involve papers published three decades ago ... Three decades is a long time from publication to retraction. But it is not a record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial delays between publication and retraction are common but problematic; timeliness in investigating and retracting erroneous or fraudulent work is important to limit harm and downstream citation. Historical examples show delays can span decades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking citation impact of retracted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The three papers have been cited a total of 33 times ... with the last such citation in 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessing how often and how recently retracted papers were cited helps gauge their ongoing influence and potential for continued harm; citation tracking should inform notification and correction efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should reference prior findings of misconduct where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The new notices do not refer to the previous findings of misconduct against Boldt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a subject has prior findings or investigations related to misconduct, retraction notices should reference relevant history to give context. Omitting prior related findings can obscure the pattern and reduce transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious misconduct may warrant legal or professional sanctions beyond retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldt’s fraudulent research did a lot of harm and he should have been prosecuted for his wilful and premeditated deceptions spread over many years. (commentary quoted on the post)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community expectations may include pursuing legal, regulatory, or professional disciplinary actions for deliberate, harmful deception. While retraction corrects the literature, other sanctions may be appropriate depending on intent and harm.
